a dense set of SNPs can be used to infer haplotypes that can be used to map complex traits in the mouse.

the dense SNP data set we developed for 10,000 evenly spaced loci across 10,000 SNPs in 48 inbred strains can be used to map phenotypes in an in silico manner and that this method can be used to refine QTL regions and identify candidate genes for further study.
the dense SNP map can be used to identify the causative polymorphism for single gene traits in the mouse, to map quantitative traits, and to identify candidate genes in QTL regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of high-resolution SNP data to map complex traits in mouse.
the use of a dense SNP set to map QTL in the mouse.
the development of new tools and methods for the in silico mapping of phenotypes to genetic variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the in silico mapping method can provide a rapid means of identifying candidate genes for complex traits and that the method is particularly useful for the identification of candidate genes in the vicinity of known QTL.
the dense SNP set and inferred haplotype model are useful in silico mapping tools that can be used to identify genes underlying phenotypic diversity.
in silico mapping using the new SNP set is a useful tool for mapping complex traits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in silico mapping can be used to rapidly identify and characterize QTL for a range of phenotypes in mice.
the dense SNP data and in silico mapping methods provide an effective way to rapidly characterize the genetics of phenotypic diversity in the mouse.
the in silico mapping of mouse phenotypes with dense SNP data is now possible and provides a valuable tool for dissecting the genetic basis of phenotypic variation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in silico mapping approach is a useful and efficient tool for identifying the genetic basis of complex phenotypes and that the dense SNP data set we generated will be useful in the future for the study of many other complex traits.
in silico mapping is an effective method to map complex genetic traits in the mouse and that dense SNP data is a necessary component to achieve this goal.
in silico mapping is a useful tool to identify and characterize genetic factors that contribute to the phenotypic variation of mice.
